stem: How is the wheel size measured and reported during a skin prick test to ensure accuracy?

options.text: By measuring the greatest wheel direction and the coordinate at $90^\circ$ to it.
By calculating the total surface area of the raised wheel using a digital scanner.
By measuring only the single largest diameter of the wheel in millimeters.
By comparing the wheel color to a standardized chromatic scale for intensity.

explanation: This method uses two axes ($X$ and $Y$ coordinates) to capture the dimensions of the reaction accurately.
rationale: Consider the two-dimensional nature of measuring an irregular shape on the skin.

optionExplanations.A: This method uses two axes ($X$ and $Y$ coordinates) to capture the dimensions of the reaction accurately.
optionExplanations.B: While technology exists, the standard clinical procedure described involves manual measurement of two specific diameters.
optionExplanations.C: Reporting only one dimension may fail to account for the irregular shapes that allergic reactions can take.
optionExplanations.D: The physical size of the wheel, rather than its color or redness, is the primary metric for reporting skin prick results.

source.hint: Consider the two-dimensional nature of measuring an irregular shape on the skin.
